observation_summary: The compiler fails to rename all instances of a function during inlining, specifically when the function is called via .call() or other indirect references, because the inliner only tracks CALL nodes.
hypothesis: The bug is in the InlineFunctions class, specifically in how it tracks function references for inlining. The current implementation only checks for CALL nodes, failing to account for other ways a function might be referenced or used, leading to incomplete renaming or inlining. The fix involves checking for NAME nodes and verifying if they are candidate usages, which ensures all references are correctly identified and updated.
prediction: The fix will broaden the reference tracking logic from just Token.CALL to include Token.NAME, ensuring all usages are captured.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff confirms that the logic was changed from checking only CALL nodes to checking NAME nodes, which is a procedural change in how the inliner identifies references to be updated.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of an incomplete search/traversal algorithm. The inliner was only looking for function calls (CALL nodes) to update references, but missed other valid references (NAME nodes) that also needed to be updated during the inlining process. This is a procedural logic error in the inlining algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check (isCandidateUsage), the primary issue is the failure of the algorithm to traverse and identify all necessary nodes for renaming, not just a missing guard.
